author: benefits_content
readerQuestion: How are SNAP and WIC different? [PAA 0/6 on-intent; 6/6 off-intent: SNAP-only shopping or Connecticut WIC; ac 32 completions include program-difference questions]
decisionGap: No lookup match, redirect or prior exact-slug history. Existing family-budget tool assigns spending but does not compare food-program eligibility. The proposed SNAP amount tool and application guide each answer a separate job, not the comparison.
finding: Reported-source synthesis of USDA program rules: the decision is often two separate applications, not choosing one winner. Map SNAP→possible WIC income qualification→remaining WIC criteria. Attribute the rules to USDA directly; do not claim we ran clinical or household eligibility tests.
conditions: Completed finite comparison table in the existing ComparisonEntry shape, five criteria with factual source-linked cells and a nonexclusive next-step paragraph. No personalized assessment, nutritional scoring or benefit-dollar comparison with an unsupported single WIC amount. Define Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children on first prose use.
whatWouldChange: A household with WIC-eligible members should check both programs rather than assume one replaces the other. SNAP receipt can simplify WIC income screening, but local WIC staff still confirm all remaining requirements. No WIC category member means the WIC application is not that household’s route.
